REQUEST
show eigenvectors as the directions a transformation does not turn, only scales, verify A v equals lambda v numerically, then show a rotation that has no real eigenvectors at all

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Most directions get knocked off their line
  2. A few come out on the same line

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, g, dirs, arrows, moved, note, pairs, lams, colours, eig_group, rows, ray, before, after

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  p(v)
  arrow(v, colour, width, opacity)
  ray(v, colour, k)
  grid()
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 3 of 4, about 20 seconds
  intent: Which is exactly what the equation says
  narration: Written down, that is A v equals lambda v: the map applied to the vector gives the same thing as simply scaling the vector. Both sides land on the same point, which the scene checks numerically before claiming it. Finding these directions means asking which vectors the map treats as mere scaling.

```python
lam, v = max(pairs, key=lambda p: p[0])
av = M.apply(v)
assert abs(av.x - lam * v.x) < 1e-12 and abs(av.y - lam * v.y) < 1e-12
self.play(FadeOut(rows), run_time=0.3)
eq = MathTex(r"A\,\vec{v}", r"=", r"\lambda\,\vec{v}",
                     font_size=40)
eq[0].set_color(EIG_C)
eq[2].set_color(EIG_C)
eq.move_to(RIGHT * 4.2 + UP * 1.8)
self.play(Write(eq), run_time=1.4)
check = VGroup(
            VGroup(MathTex(r"A\vec{v}", font_size=22, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"= ({av.x:.3f}, {av.y:.3f})", font_size=21,
                           color=EIG_C)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            VGroup(MathTex(rf"{lam:.0f}\vec{{v}}", font_size=22, color=DIM),
                   MathTex(rf"= ({lam*v.x:.3f}, {lam*v.y:.3f})", font_size=21,
                           color=EIG_C)).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            Text("same point", font_size=19, color=EIG_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
check.next_to(eq, DOWN, buff=0.55).align_to(eq, LEFT)
self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(c, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for c in check],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.6))
eq_group = VGroup(eq, check)
```
```python
self.wait(1.4)
```

REQUEST
show that a matrix is a record of where the two basis vectors land, transform the whole grid to match, and explain matrix multiplication as doing one map after another

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. The plane, and the two vectors that describe it
  2. Move only those two, and everything follows

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, grid, i_hat, j_hat, v, note, target_grid, c1, c2

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  p(v)
  grid_lines(m, colour, width, span)
  arrow(v, colour, width)
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 3 of 4, about 20 seconds
  intent: The matrix is just those two landing places
  narration: Write the two destinations side by side as columns, and that is the matrix. Not a grid of numbers with a rule bolted on — a record of where the two basis vectors went. The multiplication rule everybody learns is only the bookkeeping for rebuilding a point from its two pieces.

```python
c1, c2 = M.columns
self.play(FadeOut(note), run_time=0.3)
mat = Matrix([[f"{M.a:.0f}", f"{M.b:.0f}"],
                      [f"{M.c:.0f}", f"{M.d:.0f}"]],
                     h_buff=1.0, element_alignment_corner=ORIGIN)
mat.scale(0.9).move_to(RIGHT * 4.2 + UP * 1.7)
cols = mat.get_columns()
cols[0].set_color(I_C)
cols[1].set_color(J_C)
self.play(Write(mat), run_time=1.6)
braces = VGroup(
            Text("where i went", font_size=16, color=I_C),
            Text("where j went", font_size=16, color=J_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.16, aligned_edge=LEFT)
braces.next_to(mat, DOWN, buff=0.4)
self.play(FadeIn(braces, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.9)
work = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"{PROBE.x}\,({c1.x:.0f},{c1.y:.0f}) + "
                    rf"{PROBE.y}\,({c2.x:.0f},{c2.y:.0f})",
                    font_size=22, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"= ({M.apply(PROBE).x:.1f}, {M.apply(PROBE).y:.1f})",
                    font_size=26, color=V_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.22, aligned_edge=LEFT)
work.next_to(braces, DOWN, buff=0.5).align_to(braces, LEFT)
self.play(Write(work[0]), run_time=1.2)
self.play(FadeIn(work[1], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
mat_group = VGroup(mat, braces, work)
self.wait(1.4)
```

```python
assert verify_spread_shrinks_as_sqrt_n(KIND)
self.play(FadeOut(rows), run_time=0.3)
head = VGroup(
            Text("measured", font_size=17, color=MEAN_C),
            Text("predicted", font_size=17, color=FIT_C),
            Text("off by", font_size=17, color=DIM),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.42)
table = VGroup(head)

            got = spreads[n]
            want = raw_spread / math.sqrt(n)

            worst = max(worst, err)

                      font_size=34, color=FIT_C).next_to(table, DOWN, buff=0.6)
```

```python
self.wait(2.4)
```

REQUEST
explain the chain rule as two machines feeding into each other, work out the derivative of sine of three x plus one at a point, and show what goes wrong if the outer derivative is taken at the wrong place

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Two machines, one feeding the other

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, boxes, arrows, tags, q

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  inner(x)
  inner_prime(x)
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 2 of 4, about 27 seconds
  intent: Push a number through and watch both rates
  narration: Take x equal to nought point four. The inner machine turns it into two point two, and it does so three times as fast as x moves — nudge x by a little and u moves three times that little. Now the outer machine. Its rate is the cosine, but the cosine of what? Not of x. Of two point two, because that is the number actually arriving.

```python
g, f, prod = chain_trace(inner, inner_prime, outer, outer_prime, X0)
assert abs(g.value - 2.2) < 1e-9
assert g.rate == 3.0
self.play(FadeOut(q), run_time=0.3)
vals = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"x = {X0}", font_size=26, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"u = {g.value:.1f}", font_size=26, color=INNER_C),
            MathTex(rf"\sin u = {f.value:.4f}", font_size=24, color=OUTER_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.26, aligned_edge=LEFT)
vals.move_to(RIGHT * 3.6 + UP * 1.9)
for v in vals:
            self.play(Write(v), run_time=0.7)
rates = VGroup(
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\frac{du}{dx}", font_size=28, color=INNER_C),
                   MathTex(rf"= {g.rate:.0f}", font_size=26, color=INNER_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\cos u", font_size=28, color=OUTER_C),
                   MathTex(rf"= {f.rate:.4f}", font_size=24, color=OUTER_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
rates.next_to(vals, DOWN, buff=0.55).align_to(vals, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(rates[0], shift=LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
self.play(Indicate(boxes[0], color=INNER_C, scale_factor=1.06),
                  run_time=0.7)
self.play(FadeIn(rates[1], shift=LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
self.play(Indicate(boxes[1], color=OUTER_C, scale_factor=1.06),
                  run_time=0.7)
vals, rates = vals, rates
link = (g, f, prod)
self.wait(1.4)
```

REQUEST
explain the chain rule as two machines feeding into each other, work out the derivative of sine of three x plus one at a point, and show what goes wrong if the outer derivative is taken at the wrong place

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Two machines, one feeding the other
  2. Push a number through and watch both rates

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, boxes, arrows, tags, q, vals, rates, link, g, f, prod

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  inner(x)
  inner_prime(x)
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 3 of 4, about 20 seconds
  intent: Multiply the rates, and check it
  narration: Multiply them. Three, times the cosine of two point two, gives minus one point seven seven. That is the chain rule: the rate of the whole is the rate of the inside times the rate of the outside, taken where the inside lands. Measuring the combined function directly gives the same number.

```python
g, f, prod = link
assert verify_chain_rule(inner, inner_prime, outer, outer_prime,
                                 [-1, 0, X0, 1, 2])
num = numeric_derivative(lambda t: outer(inner(t)), X0)
assert abs(prod - num) < 1e-5
assert round(prod, 2) == -1.77
product = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"{g.rate:.0f} \times {f.rate:.4f}", font_size=28,
                    color=PROD_C),
            MathTex(rf"= {prod:.4f}", font_size=32, color=PROD_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
product.next_to(rates, DOWN, buff=0.55).align_to(rates, LEFT)
self.play(Write(product[0]), run_time=1.1)
self.play(FadeIn(product[1], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
check = VGroup(
            Text("measured directly", font_size=18, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"{num:.4f}", font_size=24, color=PROD_C),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN)
check.next_to(product, DOWN, buff=0.4).align_to(product, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(check), run_time=0.9)
product, check = product, check
self.wait(1.6)
```

REQUEST
explain the chain rule as two machines feeding into each other, work out the derivative of sine of three x plus one at a point, and show what goes wrong if the outer derivative is taken at the wrong place

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Two machines, one feeding the other
  2. Push a number through and watch both rates
  3. Multiply the rates, and check it

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, boxes, arrows, tags, q, vals, rates, link, g, f, prod, num, product, check

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  inner(x)
  inner_prime(x)
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 4 of 4, about 26 seconds
  intent: The mistake everyone makes, and what it costs
  narration: Here is the error worth seeing. Take the cosine of x rather than of u — cosine of nought point four rather than of two point two — and multiply by three. That gives plus two point seven six. Not slightly off: the wrong sign. The function is falling and the answer says it is rising, because the outer rate was read at the wrong place.

```python
g, f, prod = link
wrong = outer_prime(X0) * inner_prime(X0)
assert round(wrong, 2) == 2.76
assert wrong * prod < 0
self.play(FadeOut(vals), FadeOut(rates), FadeOut(check),
                  run_time=0.5)
self.play(product.animate.scale(0.9).move_to(
            RIGHT * 3.6 + UP * 1.9), run_time=0.7)
bad = VGroup(
            Text("reading cos at x, not u", font_size=19, color=BAD_C),
            MathTex(rf"\cos({X0}) \times {g.rate:.0f}", font_size=26, color=BAD_C),
            MathTex(rf"= {wrong:+.4f}", font_size=30, color=BAD_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
bad.next_to(product, DOWN, buff=0.65).align_to(product, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(bad[0]), run_time=0.7)
self.play(Write(bad[1]), run_time=1.0)
self.play(FadeIn(bad[2], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
self.play(Indicate(bad[2], color=BAD_C, scale_factor=1.15), run_time=0.9)
verdict = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"{prod:+.2f}", font_size=28, color=PROD_C),
            Text("vs", font_size=18, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"{wrong:+.2f}", font_size=28, color=BAD_C),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
note = Text("opposite sign", font_size=21, color=BAD_C)
tail = VGroup(verdict, note).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=LEFT)
tail.next_to(bad, DOWN, buff=0.5).align_to(bad, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(tail, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=1.0)
self.wait(2.4)
```

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Two machines, one feeding the other

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, boxes, arrows, tags, q

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  inner(x)
  inner_prime(x)
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 2 of 4, about 27 seconds
  intent: Push a number through and watch both rates
  narration: Take x equal to nought point four. The inner machine turns it into two point two, and it does so three times as fast as x moves — nudge x by a little and u moves three times that little. Now the outer machine. Its rate is the cosine, but the cosine of what? Not of x. Of two point two, because that is the number actually arriving.

```python
g, f, prod = chain_trace(inner, inner_prime, outer, outer_prime, X0)
assert abs(g.value - 2.2) < 1e-9
assert g.rate == 3.0
self.play(FadeOut(q), run_time=0.3)

            MathTex(rf"x = {X0}", font_size=26, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"u = {g.value:.1f}", font_size=26, color=INNER_C),
            MathTex(rf"\sin u = {f.value:.4f}", font_size=24, color=OUTER_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.26, aligned_edge=LEFT)
vals.move_to(RIGHT * 3.6 + UP * 1.9)
for v in vals:
            self.play(Write(v), run_time=0.7)
rates = VGroup(
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\frac{du}{dx}", font_size=28, color=INNER_C),
                   MathTex(rf"= {g.rate:.0f}", font_size=26, color=INNER_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
            VGroup(MathTex(r"\cos u", font_size=28, color=OUTER_C),
                   MathTex(rf"= {f.rate:.4f}", font_size=24, color=OUTER_C)
                   ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3, aligned_edge=LEFT)
rates.next_to(vals, DOWN, buff=0.55).align_to(vals, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(rates[0], shift=LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
self.play(Indicate(boxes[0], color=INNER_C, scale_factor=1.06),
                  run_time=0.7)
self.play(FadeIn(rates[1], shift=LEFT * 0.2), run_time=0.8)
self.play(Indicate(boxes[1], color=OUTER_C, scale_factor=1.06),
                  run_time=0.7)
vals, rates = vals, rates
link = (g, f, prod)
self.wait(1.4)
```

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 3 of 4, about 20 seconds
  intent: Multiply the rates, and check it
  narration: Multiply them. Three, times the cosine of two point two, gives minus one point seven seven.
```python
g, f, prod = link

                                 [-1, 0, X0, 1, 2])

assert round(prod, 2) == -1.77

            MathTex(rf"{g.rate:.0f} \times {f.rate:.4f}", font_size=28,
                    color=PROD_C),
            MathTex(rf"= {prod:.4f}", font_size=32, color=PROD_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
product.next_to(rates, DOWN, buff=0.55).align_to(rates, LEFT)
self.play(Write(product[0]), run_time=1.1)
self.play(FadeIn(product[1], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
check = VGroup(
            Text("measured directly", font_size=18, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"{num:.4f}", font_size=24, color=PROD_C),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=DOWN)
check.next_to(product, DOWN, buff=0.4).align_to(product, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(check), run_time=0.9)
product, check = product, check
self.wait(1.6)
```

REQUEST
explain the chain rule as two machines feeding into each other, work out the derivative of sine of three x plus one at a point, and show what goes wrong if the outer derivative is taken at the wrong place

ALREADY ON SCREEN
  1. Two machines, one feeding the other
  2. Push a number through and watch both rates
  3. Multiply the rates, and check it

NAMES IN SCOPE
  title, boxes, arrows, tags, q, vals, rates, link, g, f, prod, num, product, check

HELPERS THIS SCENE DEFINES
  inner(x)
  inner_prime(x)
  panel()

WRITE THIS BEAT — step 4 of 4, about 26 seconds
  intent: The mistake everyone makes, and what it costs
  narration: Here is the error worth seeing. Take the cosine of x rather than of u — cosine of nought point four rather than of two point two — and multiply by three. That gives plus two point seven six. Not slightly off: the wrong sign. The function is falling and the answer says it is rising, because the outer rate was read at the wrong place.

```python
g, f, prod = link
wrong = outer_prime(X0) * inner_prime(X0)
assert round(wrong, 2) == 2.76
assert wrong * prod < 0
self.play(FadeOut(vals), FadeOut(rates), FadeOut(check),
                  run_time=0.5)
self.play(product.animate.scale(0.9).move_to(
            RIGHT * 3.6 + UP * 1.9), run_time=0.7)
bad = VGroup(
            Text("reading cos at x, not u", font_size=19, color=BAD_C),
            MathTex(rf"\cos({X0}) \times {g.rate:.0f}", font_size=26, color=BAD_C),
            MathTex(rf"= {wrong:+.4f}", font_size=30, color=BAD_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.24, aligned_edge=LEFT)
bad.next_to(product, DOWN, buff=0.65).align_to(product, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(bad[0]), run_time=0.7)
self.play(Write(bad[1]), run_time=1.0)
self.play(FadeIn(bad[2], shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
self.play(Indicate(bad[2], color=BAD_C, scale_factor=1.15), run_time=0.9)
verdict = VGroup(
            MathTex(rf"{prod:+.2f}", font_size=28, color=PROD_C),
            Text("vs", font_size=18, color=DIM),
            MathTex(rf"{wrong:+.2f}", font_size=28, color=BAD_C),
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
note = Text("opposite sign", font_size=21, color=BAD_C)
tail = VGroup(verdict, note).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.25, aligned_edge=LEFT)
tail.next_to(bad, DOWN, buff=0.5).align_to(bad, LEFT)
self.play(FadeIn(tail, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=1.0)
```
```python
self.wait(2.4)
```

```python
rows = VGroup()
for m, k, note in ((1.0, 4.0, "baseline"),
                           (4.0, 4.0, "4x the mass"),
                           (1.0, 16.0, "4x the stiffness")):
            sm = SpringMass(mass=m, stiffness=k)
            rows.add(VGroup(
                Text(note, font_size=21, color=DIM),
                Text(f"{sm.period:.2f}s", font_size=26, color=TRACE_C),
            ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.35, aligned_edge=DOWN))
rows.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.26, aligned_edge=LEFT)
rows.to_edge(RIGHT, buff=0.7).shift(UP * 1.4)
formula = MathTex(r"T = 2\pi\sqrt{\tfrac{m}{k}}", font_size=40, color=TRACE_C)
formula.next_to(rows, DOWN, buff=0.45)
self.play(curve.animate.set_stroke(opacity=1.0), run_time=0.4)
self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(r, shift=LEFT * 0.2) for r in rows],
                              lag_ratio=0.3, run_time=1.6))
self.play(Write(formula), run_time=1.2)
self.wait(1.6)
```

```python
                              lag_ratio=0.2, run_time=1.4))
closing = VGroup(
            Text("never zero,", font_size=22, color=INT_C),
            Text("never the last one", font_size=22, color=INT_C),
        ).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1).next_to(rows, DOWN, buff=0.35)
self.play(FadeIn(closing, shift=UP * 0.12), run_time=0.8)
self.wait(1.4)
```

```python
marks = VGroup()

            row = VGroup()
            for num in range(-4 * den, 4 * den + 1):
                f = Fraction(num, den)
                if f.denominator != den:        # already drawn at a coarser step
                    continue
                row.add(Line(line.n2p(float(f)) + DOWN * 0.11,
                             line.n2p(float(f)) + UP * 0.11,
                             color=FRAC_C, stroke_width=2).set_opacity(0.8))

            self.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(m) for m in row],
                                  lag_ratio=0.01, run_time=1.2))
label = MathTex(r"\tfrac{1}{2},\ \tfrac{1}{4},\ \tfrac{1}{8},\ \dots",
                        font_size=34, color=FRAC_C).next_to(line, DOWN, buff=0.9)
self.play(Write(label), run_time=0.9)
marks, frac_label = marks, label
self.wait(0.8)
```

```python
sq_group = VGroup(dot, lab)
```
```python
self.wait(0.9)
```

```python
num_points = 100
oscillatory_circle_points = []
for i in range(num_points):
            theta = i * 2 * PI / num_points
            # Add oscillations to the radius
            radius = 2 + 0.3 * np.sin(8 * theta)
            x = radius * np.cos(theta)
            y = radius * np.sin(theta)
            oscillatory_circle_points.append([x, y, 0])
oscillatory_circle = Polygon(*oscillatory_circle_points, color=PURPLE)

for y in np.arange(-2, 2.1, 0.5):
            wavy_line = VMobject(color=BLUE_E)
            points = []
            for x in np.arange(-2, 2.1, 0.1):
                # Simple wave distortion
                new_y = y + 0.2 * np.sin(3 * x) * np.exp(-0.5 * (x**2 + y**2))
                points.append([x, new_y, 0])
            wavy_line.set_points_as_corners(points)
            distorted_grid.add(wavy_line)
for x in np.arange(-2, 2.1, 0.5):

            points = []
            for y in np.arange(-2, 2.1, 0.1):
                # Simple wave distortion
                new_x = x + 0.2 * np.sin(3 * y) * np.exp(-0.5 * (x**2 + y**2))
                points.append([new_x, y, 0])
            wavy_line.set_points_as_corners(points)
            distorted_grid.add(wavy_line)
self.play(ReplacementTransform(grid, distorted_grid), run_time=2)
self.wait(1)
```

```python
            points = []

                # The closer to the end, the closer to the mean
                if i == 0:
```

```python
title = Text("Cracking the Coverage Code: Probability on a 3x3 Grid", font_size=28)
title.to_edge(UP)
self.play(FadeIn(title))
grid = VGroup()
for i in range(4):
            h_line = Line([-1.5, -1.5 + i, 0], [1.5, -1.5 + i, 0])
            grid.add(h_line)
for i in range(4):
            v_line = Line([-1.5 + i, -1.5, 0], [-1.5 + i, 1.5, 0])
            grid.add(v_line)
nodes = VGroup()
for i in range(3):
            for j in range(3):
                node = Dot([-1 + i, -1 + j, 0], color=RED)
                nodes.add(node)
self.play(Create(grid), Create(nodes))
walker = Dot([-1, -1, 0], color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
self.play(FadeIn(walker))
nodes[0].set_color(GREEN)
moves = [
            [-1, 0, 0],  # Move up
            [0, 0, 0],   # Move right
            [0, 1, 0],   # Move up
            [1, 1, 0],   # Move right
            [1, 0, 0],   # Move down
        ]
for i, move in enumerate(moves):
            self.play(walker.animate.move_to(move), run_time=0.5)
            
            # Mark visited nodes
            for j, node in enumerate(nodes):
                if np.allclose(node.get_center(), move):
                    nodes[j].set_color(GREEN)
hit_time_text = Text("Hit Time:", font_size=24)
hit_time_text.next_to(grid, DOWN, buff=0.5)
self.play(Write(hit_time_text))
hit_time_eq = MathTex(r"H(n_i) = \text{Expected steps to revisit } n_i")
hit_time_eq.next_to(hit_time_text, RIGHT, buff=0.3)
self.play(Write(hit_time_eq))
self.wait(1)
```

```python
bm_title = Text("Block Maxima Approach", color=BLUE).next_to(title, DOWN)
self.play(Write(bm_title))
blocks = VGroup()
max_dots = VGroup()
for i in range(3):
            # Block boundaries
            x_start = i * 3.33
            x_end = (i + 1) * 3.33
            
            # Create visual block
            block = Rectangle(
                width=3.33 * axes.x_axis.unit_size,
                height=4 * axes.y_axis.unit_size,
                fill_color=BLUE,
                fill_opacity=0.2,
                stroke_width=1
            ).move_to(axes.c2p((x_start + x_end)/2, 0))
            blocks.add(block)
            
            # Find maximum in this block
            block_indices = (x_values >= x_start) & (x_values < x_end)
            if np.any(block_indices):
                block_y = y_values[block_indices]
                max_idx = np.argmax(block_y)
                max_x = x_values[block_indices][max_idx]
                max_y = block_y[max_idx]
                
                # Create dot for maximum
                max_dot = Dot(axes.c2p(max_x, max_y), color=BLUE, radius=0.1)
                max_dots.add(max_dot)
self.play(Create(blocks))
self.play(Create(max_dots))
bm_eq = MathTex("M_n = \\max(X_1, X_2, \\ldots, X_n)")
self.play(Write(bm_eq.next_to(bm_title, DOWN)))
self.wait(1)
```
